checks.says: Every block is a tile: flat, opaque, no border, no shadow, radius 16, on one flat board colour. Nothing floats on the board but the header.
The rail is the board's flat left column, the same colour as the board, with the chosen place as a tile-coloured fill.
The header is the page's name at 28px and one headline sentence at 17px, with no card around it.
One red working accent for selection, primary buttons, links and charts. Late and needs-you take the deeper red with a mark or a word, never the colour alone.
Buttons are rectangles with radius 8. Pills only for counts. No dashed chips.
Every list sits inside a tile, and a tile holds no tile.
Tiles sit on a grid of 12 columns and span 3, 4, 6, 8 or 12, one gap apart, full width with fluid gutters.
Geist at 13, 15, 17, 22 and 28 only, weights 400, 500 and 600, body text 15px or more, tabular figures for money.
A chart is drawn only when it has three points and says something; otherwise the tile shows the number.
Names, never ids: no raw id, handle, file path, raw time or placeholder in anything a person reads, and no em dash.
At 390 the same board is one column with 12px side gutters, the header at 22px, a flat bottom bar and nothing sideways.
No glass, gradients, glows, two-tone headings, chip clouds or feature-card grids. Fewer things on screen, not more.
